items.prompt: Black has just moved a rook to e8 and said nothing. It is White's turn. Which move is allowed?

claims.statement: White is in check, although no one said the word.
The only legal moves are Kd1, Kd2 and Kf1.
The pawn move a3 is illegal: it leaves the king attacked.

hints: Look at the e-file between the black rook and the white king.
Is the white king attacked right now? Does that depend on anyone saying it?
Only king moves leave the e-file; count the safe squares next to the king.
items.explain: The rook on e8 attacks the king on e1 along an open file, so White is in check whether or not anyone announces it. Calling out 'check' is a courtesy and not a rule. The validator confirms the check and that only Kd1, Kd2 and Kf1 are legal.

feedback_by_move.a2a3: a3 is illegal. The king is attacked by the rook on e8, and the rule applies even though Black said nothing, so only a move that ends the check is allowed.

items.prompt: White is in check and cannot simply step aside. What is the only legal move?

claims.statement: White is in check.
Rxe1 is White's only legal move.
Kh1 is illegal: the rook on e1 still attacks it along the first rank.
Kf1 is illegal: it steps next to the rook on e1, which is attacking that square.

hints: List the squares next to the white king and mark which are blocked or attacked.
The pawns block the second rank. What does the black rook attack along the first rank?
Another white piece can deal with the checking rook.
items.explain: The pawns shut the second rank, and the rook on e1 attacks the squares f1 and h1 along the rank, so the king has nowhere to go. A king in check cannot always step away. The rook on c1 can capture the checking piece, and the validator confirms that Rxe1 is the only legal move.

feedback_by_move.g1h1: Kh1 is illegal. The king would leave g1 but stay on the first rank, where the rook on e1 still attacks it.
feedback_by_move.g1f1: Kf1 is illegal. The square is attacked by the rook on e1.

items.prompt: White is in check from a knight. Someone says 'just block it'. Which of these moves is legal: Qe1, Qxf3, gxf3, Kh1, Kf1?

claims.statement: White is in check from the knight on f3.
The legal moves are Qxf3, gxf3, Kh1 and Kf1.
Qe1 is illegal; the check is still there afterwards.

hints: The knight on f3 and the king on g1 are not on one line. What would a blocking piece stand on?
A knight jumps. Is there any square between f3 and g1 that a piece could occupy to cut the attack?
Look for a capture of the knight, or a king move.
items.explain: A knight attacks by jumping, so there is no line to cut and no blocking move exists. White must capture the knight (Qxf3 or gxf3) or move the king (Kh1 or Kf1). The validator confirms these four are the only legal moves, and that Qe1 is illegal.

feedback_by_move.d1e1: Qe1 is illegal. Putting a piece next to the king does not stop a knight, which jumps. The only answers to this check are to capture the knight or to move the king.

items.prompt: A game review tagged White's king move here as 'calculation error'. Before you accept the tag, find the one move that keeps the win.

claims.statement: After e4 White still wins.
After Kb6 the position is a draw.
After Kb5 the position is a draw.

hints: Is the position about a long tactic, or about what a king and a pawn can do on their own?
Count how many king moves keep the win. Does a long calculation help, or does a known idea?
The pawn is the only piece that can make progress by itself.
items.explain: The tablebase shows that e4 wins while every king move only draws. The position has no tactic to miss, so the label 'calculation error' is a guess; asking 'what would I have needed to know here?' is the question that tests it. The label does not settle the cause on its own.

feedback_by_move.a6b6: Kb6 is a draw according to the tablebase. The mistake here is not a missed tactic, so ask what knowledge was missing before you call it a calculation error.
feedback_by_move.a6b5: Kb5 is a draw according to the tablebase. A label is a question to ask, not a diagnosis.

items.prompt: Black to move. Rxh5 wins a pawn and you cannot see a defence for White. Before you play it, test it against the opponent's best reply: which move is best?

claims.statement: Rxb4+ is the engine's best move.
Rxh5 is much worse than the best move.

hints: Name White's best reply to the pawn grab before you count the pawn.
Look at the captures and checks Black has, not only the one that wins a pawn.
One of the checks takes a piece that is attacking Black's rook.
items.explain: Not seeing a defence is not proof that there is none: the engine rates Rxh5 at least 300 centipawns below Rxb4+. Check the opponent's best reply before you count on the pawn. Engine evidence at depth 16; it is not a proof.

feedback_by_move.h4h5: Rxh5 wins a pawn, but the engine rates it at least 300 centipawns worse than Rxb4+. Not seeing a defence did not mean there was none.

items.prompt: Black to move. A line that starts with the check d3+ expects White to answer in one particular way. Test what White can actually do, and find the best move.

claims.statement: dxc3 is the engine's best move.
d3+ is much worse than the best move.

hints: Which pieces can answer the check on d3, and not only the king stepping away?
A pawn on d3 stands next to the white king. What can the king do about it?
Compare the check with the capture of the knight.
items.explain: A check is only as good as the opponent's best reply to it. The engine rates d3+ at least 300 centipawns below dxc3, so a line that needs White to cooperate fails. Engine evidence at depth 16.

feedback_by_move.d4d3: d3+ gives check, but the engine rates it at least 300 centipawns worse than dxc3. The line only works if White chooses the reply you expect.

items.prompt: A detector labels any move that leaves your queen attacked and undefended as 'hung a piece'. Black to move: find the best move, then say whether that label would be a fair diagnosis here.

claims.statement: Qxb3 is the engine's best move.
After Qxb3 the queen on b3 is attacked and undefended (the pawn on a5 also).
Bxg5 is much worse than the best move.

hints: Count which black pieces are attacked and undefended after each candidate.
A label looks at one feature. What does the move win or threaten that the label does not see?
Look at the white knight on b3.
items.explain: After Qxb3 the queen is attacked and undefended, so the detector's label would fire, yet the engine rates Qxb3 as best. The label points to a question (what does this move win?), not to the cause. Engine evidence at depth 16.

feedback_by_move.e7g5: Bxg5 avoids leaving a piece loose, but the engine rates it at least 300 centipawns below Qxb3. A label that fires on Qxb3 is a prompt to ask a question, not a verdict.

items.prompt: Black to move. Write the move and one feature of the position that makes it work. 'I take the knight' only restates the move; name something about the position.

claims.statement: Bxe2 is the engine's best move.
The knight on e2 is White's only loose piece: attacked and undefended.
Rxc1+ is much worse than the best move.

hints: Which white pieces are attacked? Which of them has no defender?
Name the square of the attacked piece and say who defends it.
Compare the capture of the rook with the capture of the knight.
items.explain: A good explanation names a feature: the knight on e2 is attacked by the bishop and no white piece defends it. 'I take the knight' restates the move and gives you nothing to check. The validator confirms the knight is White's only loose piece.

feedback_by_move.c7c1: Rxc1+ is a capture with check, but the engine rates it at least 300 centipawns below Bxe2. 'It is a check' names a feature, but the feature has to hold up when you test it.

items.prompt: Your opportunity log says 'forks: three available, three taken'. Three chances are a small sample, so call it 'worth checking', not a trait. Here is a fourth chance. White to move: find the best move.

claims.statement: Nc7+ is the engine's best move.
From c7 the knight attacks the king on e8 and the rook on a8.
Nc7+ wins at least two points of material.
Nxf6+ is much worse than the best move.

hints: Which black pieces can a knight on c7 attack?
The king is one of them. Name the other.
Compare the check on f6 with the check on c7.
items.explain: Nc7+ attacks the king and the rook on a8 at once. One more chance changes the count to four taken, but a rate from four chances is still a small sample: it says 'worth checking', not 'you are good at forks'. Engine evidence at depth 16.

feedback_by_move.d5f6: Nxf6+ gives check and takes a bishop, but the engine rates it at least 300 centipawns below Nc7+. Missing the fork would also be one more data point, and a small one.

items.prompt: Your budget gave every move two minutes. This is a critical moment in a pawn ending: Kxb6 wins a pawn at once. Which move is best?

claims.statement: d4 is the engine's best move.
Kxb6 is much worse than the best move.

hints: Before you spend time, ask whether this move is routine or critical.
The pawn grab is the first move you see. What else can the pawns do?
The move is a pawn move that changes the structure.
items.explain: The obvious pawn grab is at least 300 centipawns worse than d4 according to the engine. Positions like this deserve more of the clock than a routine move, which is why a budget that gives every move the same time is not a real budget. Engine evidence at depth 16.

feedback_by_move.b7b6: Kxb6 wins a pawn, but the engine rates it at least 300 centipawns below d4. A critical moment is where extra time pays off.

items.prompt: Black has a bishop against a rook, and the bishop is attacked. Which moves keep the draw?

claims.statement: After Bc6 the position is a draw.
After Bd7 the position is a draw.
After Bf7 the position is a draw.
After Bh5 Black loses.
After Bg6 Black loses.

hints: A rook is stronger than a bishop in the open, but the game is about whether the bishop can be won.
Which squares does the rook on g8 attack?
Pick a square the rook does not attack.
items.explain: The extra rook does not win by itself. If the bishop reaches a square the rook does not attack, the position is a draw according to the tablebase, and Bh5 and Bg6 lose. So 'a rook beats a bishop' is not a rule: it depends on whether the bishop can be caught.

feedback_by_move.e8h5: Bh5 loses according to the tablebase. A rook does not always beat a bishop, but a bishop on an attacked square can be lost.
feedback_by_move.e8g6: Bg6 loses according to the tablebase. The bishop stays on a square the rook attacks.
